title: Tamsin and the Escarpment
premise: Marguerite Yarrow, estranged daughter of disgraced archaeologist Edmund Yarrow, is scraping a living as a wilderness guide when a dying prospector presses a hand-drawn map into her hands and extracts a promise: deliver it to the escarpment above the Kettle Glacier before calving season seals the route. The map points to a pre-contact site that could restore her father's ruined reputation — or destroy what remains of his integrity, because the artifacts there are being hunted by his expedition's financier, who intends to sell them privately. Marguerite joins the expedition under a false name to protect the site and confronts the father who abandoned her. In the end she exposes the financier, chooses truth over loyalty by testifying against her father's complicity, and leads the surviving team out through the glacier corridor in a final race ahead of the calving.
about_author: V. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former field surveyor who spent six seasons mapping glacial routes in the northern ranges before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people whose competence is their only armor.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Promise
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Guiding a wealthy client through the river country, she finds prospector Aldous Crane gut-shot in an abandoned trapper's cabin. He trades her a grease-pencil map for a promise to carry it to the escarpment before the melt. Beat: reluctant inheritance; grief for a stranger who trusted her.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She studies the map and recognizes her father's survey notations from childhood lessons — handwriting she swore she'd forgotten. A newspaper clipping reveals Yarrow's new expedition is funded by mining magnate Corliss Vane. Beat: old wounds reopened; the pull between walking away and walking in.

chapters.title: Hired Under a False Sky
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Using her mother's surname, she talks her way onto Vane's expedition as a route-finder. She meets geologist Priya Nair, cook Tomás Reyes, and Vane himself — charming, watchful, wrong. Beat: tension of disguise; first spark of found-family belonging with Priya and Tomás.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Me Stone
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Edmund Yarrow recognizes her digging style before he recognizes her face. Their first confrontation on the trail is cold, professional, devastating. Beat: anger sharpened into control; she decides to stay close precisely because it hurts.

chapters.title: Corliss Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya notices Vane's supply manifests don't match an archaeological dig — crates, chains, a private helicopter fuel cache. She shares her suspicion with Marguerite over watch duty. Beat: alliance formed; the expedition's true purpose begins to surface.

chapters.title: The Kettle Crossing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The team crosses the glacier's lower tongue; a crevasse collapse nearly takes Tomás, saved by Marguerite's quick anchor work. Edmund watches his daughter save a life with techniques he taught her. Beat: competence as love language; grudging respect cracking the estrangement.

chapters.title: Camp at the Scree Line
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Around the fire, stories are traded; Tomás tells why he came — money for his sister's surgery — and Marguerite almost tells the truth about who she is. Beat: warmth before the storm; the found family solidifies while secrets calcify.

chapters.title: Vane's Advance Party
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers Vane sent four armed men ahead along the eastern moraine toward the escarpment — days before any legitimate survey would go there. Beat: dread; the promise Marguerite made now has a deadline enforced by guns.

chapters.title: Night Run
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She slips camp at night to reach the escarpment approach first, intending to warn whoever guards the site. Edmund catches her at the rope line — and instead of stopping her, comes with her. Beat: uneasy partnership; two liars moving toward one truth.

chapters.title: The Escarpment
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They reach the ledge and find the site: intact carvings, a buried longhouse, evidence of a sophisticated trade culture history erased. Edmund is transformed by wonder — and then ashamed, knowing what Vane will do here. Beat: awe braided with guilt; father and daughter briefly aligned.

chapters.title: What Edmund Buried
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Flashback-weighted chapter: how Vane bought him after his disgrace, what he agreed to look away from, and why he let his daughter believe she was abandoned to protect her from Vane's leverage. Beat: tragic revelation; sympathy without absolution.

chapters.title: The First Theft
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Vane's advance party reaches the site and begins crating carvings for airlift. Priya photographs everything and radios Marguerite — but Vane intercepts the transmission and now knows there's a leak. Beat: point of no return; the quiet phase ends.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Vane detains Tomás and Priya as 'logistical witnesses,' confiscating equipment. Tomás realizes Marguerite's false name won't survive interrogation and sends a coded warning via the camp's supply runner. Beat: fear and loyalty; the family scatters but holds.

chapters.title: Marguerite Falls
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Confronted by Vane's men on the descent, she escapes down a rotten gully, breaking her wrist and losing the map — which Vane now possesses. Beat: despair at its floor; the promise seems broken, the advantage lost.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Second Gift
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund reveals Crane was his old partner and the map has a duplicate key: coordinates memorized, not drawn. He offers Marguerite the truth and asks for nothing but the chance to fix it. Beat: fragile trust rebuilt on shared purpose rather than blood.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The glacier begins to calve early; the exit corridor will close within days. Vane orders the helicopter lifts regardless, gambling lives for cargo. Priya sabotages the fuel cache and is caught. Beat: sacrifice; the cost of resistance becomes personal and visible.

chapters.title: The Longhouse Stand
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite, Edmund, and freed Tomás retake the site at dawn, using terrain knowledge against Vane's armed crew. Edmund stands publicly against Vane for the first time, recording his confession of the arrangement. Beat: courage; loyalty finally pointed at truth instead of survival.

chapters.title: Whiteout Bargain
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Storm and icefall trap both sides. Vane, injured, bargains: safe extraction for everyone if the crates go with him. Marguerite counters — the man goes free, the artifacts stay, documented and reported. Beat: moral climax; power confronted with terms it cannot buy.

chapters.title: The Corridor Closes
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. The race out through the narrowing glacier corridor as seracs fall behind them; Priya, injured but mobile, navigates by memory. They emerge as the route collapses into the lake. Beat: catharsis; survival earned together, no one left behind.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Weeks later, at the inquiry, Marguerite testifies fully — including her father's complicity — even though it ends whatever reconciliation they might have had. Edmund thanks her for telling the truth. Beat: bittersweet integrity; loyalty to truth chosen over loyalty to blood.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The site is protected as heritage land; Priya publishes the documentation with full attribution to the descendant communities. Vane faces charges; Tomás's sister gets her surgery. Beat: restoration; the world set slightly more right.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Escarpment
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite returns to the escarpment with a small permitted team — including her father, invited as a consultant, nothing more. At the carved threshold she leaves Crane's compass. Beat: quiet resolution; forgiveness as an open door, not a settled debt.
